analysis:
The supplied units are BASE text for StandaloneServer.swift lines 1-1219. The changed head ranges (about lines 1538-1564) are visible only in the patch excerpt, not in these units. The patch adds a one-time reclaim step to the memory-headroom wait loop that runs before LRU eviction. It calls GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments() and MLX.Memory.clearCache(), the latter only if nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed. The reclaim is gated on !GlobalKVCacheBudget.busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory(). The patch's own comment says this drops retained free KV segments and the MLX buffer pool. These are memory-hygiene operations that run before an eviction, so they reduce pressure on A-001 and T-028 residue. They do not widen exposure.

Security-relevant checks:
- The change adds no new attack surface or at-rest artifact. The T-041 SSD prefix cache, its HMAC naming, TTL and salt scoping are untouched by the patch.
- The change does not alter authentication, authorization or encryption. It adds no new data exposure path.
- The cache-clear call keeps the nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed guard, consistent with the other call sites in the base text (lines 729-732, 1181).
- The new function runs inside the isLoadingAny critical section like the existing loop, so the load-gate serialization is preserved.
- A possible availability concern is that clearCache could race with in-flight native MiMo work. The guard addresses this, and I cannot verify the semantics of releaseRetainedKVSegments or busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory because they are outside the supplied evidence. Their definitions and any waiting or timeout behavior need a look from the integration pass. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.

No concrete regression identified.
